# Gravity compensation holds arm, but dragging is stiff: KD, MIT mode, and structural load discussion

> **Current answer:** High KD will directly convert joint velocity into damping torque, which can hold the arm but may damage the anti-jerk feeling. Verify the gravity model and friction first, then reduce KD and record tau/velocity/current in the limit/secure mode; handle structural load issues separately. The post does not provide final parameters.

## Problem and symptoms

- Gravity compensation holds the arm, but dragging is stiff; why can't KD be increased directly?
- Arm can hold, but J2/J3 damping feels strong and downward dragging is not smooth.

## Environment

- 6-axis mechanical arm; MIT control; J2 kd=0.8, others ~0.1/0.

## Possible causes

- J2 kd too large, directly increasing speed damping; near-end joint load and model compensation error may force users to use high kd to dampen vibration.

## Attempts

- Author used kp=0, small kd, and gravity compensation; comments discussed bringing J4 close to J3 to reduce load.
